# Preface {.unnumbered}

The Lord's Prayer is the one text that most of Christendom says in its own
language while believing it is saying the same thing. This book sets six of
those languages side by side, one to a chapter, so the shared skeleton is easy
to see: the address to the Father, the three wishes, the four requests.

Each chapter gives the text as Wikipedia records it, the tradition it comes
from, and — where the script is not Latin — a transliteration printed under
each line.

## Reading the Greek chapters

The two Greek chapters print a transliteration in the Latin alphabet beneath
each line of Greek:

::: {.prayer lang="grc" speech="el-GR" #demo}
| Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς
| [Páter hēmôn ho en toîs ouranoîs]{.tr}
:::

The **Hide transliteration** button above the text removes those lines. The
choice is remembered across chapters and across visits, so you can read the
Greek unaided once you no longer need the crutch.

The two Greek chapters transliterate to different targets, and it is worth
knowing which you are looking at. The Ancient Greek chapter uses Wikipedia's
scholarly romanisation, which encodes the *spelling* — vowel length, breathings,
pitch accents. The Modern Greek chapter transliterates the *sound* of the text
as it is spoken in Greece today. The same written word therefore comes out
differently in the two chapters, which is the point.

## The six chapters

| Chapter | Text |
|---|---|
| [Spanish](chapters/spanish.qmd) | Scío / Reina-Valera, with the liturgical variant |
| [Lithuanian](chapters/lithuanian.qmd) | Catholic and Orthodox forms |
| [English](chapters/english.qmd) | BCP 1662, traditional ecumenical, ELLC 1988 |
| [Ancient Greek](chapters/ancient-greek.qmd) | The Koine original, NA28 and Patriarchal 1904 |
| [Modern Greek](chapters/modern-greek.qmd) | The demotic rendering |
| [Latin](chapters/latin.qmd) | Roman Missal and Vulgata Clementina |

Full provenance for every text is in [Sources](chapters/sources.qmd).
